findings.summary: The sign-in continuation now accepts (consumes) the invitation, which contradicts the normative requirement that login continuation must preserve a validated invitation without consuming it.
findings.evidence: Diff: "Login continuation from an invitation accepts it for the invitee once sign-in succeeds" vs S.webapp.authentication: "Login continuation must preserve a validated invitation without consuming it."

findings.summary: The J.connect journey still routes signed-out invitees through sign-in with the invitation preserved and then to an explicit Accept/Decline step, which conflicts with one-tap acceptance at sign-in and the new ConsentPanel description limiting it to already-signed-in invitees.
findings.evidence: J.connect s6: "Sign in; the validated invitation is preserved and not consumed" -> s7 "See who is inviting; Accept or Decline"; ConsentPanel: "Shown to invitees who open the invitation while already signed in".

findings.summary: Acceptance at sign-in bypasses the explicit Accept consent and the operation.invite.accept path (no invokes link, no block/self-connection/decline handling), weakening the explicit two-consent model the system relies on.
findings.evidence: policy.pairConsent: "creating the invitation and accepting it provide the two consents"; ConsentPanel.accept is the only affordance invoking operation.invite.accept, while the changed Continue affordance has only a references link to ext.providers.
